newsitem.title: USA: House votes to end federal arts funding.
newsitem.headline: House votes to end federal arts funding.

text.p: The House of Representatives moved Friday to close the National Endowment for the Arts and rejected a plan to continue federal funding for the arts through block grants to states and school districts.

The House voted 271 to 155 against a compromise offered by House Republicans to continue federal arts funding through block grants. Democrats and some moderate Republicans refused to vote for a scheme to shut down the NEA and some conservative Republicans balked at continuing any federal arts funding.

Despite the House vote, advocates of the NEA -- which distributes grants to community orchestras, theater troups, writers, sculptors and other artists -- said they expected the agency would be saved by the Senate and the White House.
"On the Senate side, we're a lot more optimistic that the NEA will be retained," said Elliot Mincberg, vice president of the People for the American Way Action Fund.

The House voted 217-216 Thursday to back a Republican effort to abolish the NEA. Because the vote was so close and because of expected support in the Senate, Mincberg and several House Democrats said they were optimistic the final bill to emerge from Congress would continue the agency.
The Clinton administration has threatened to veto a $13 billion bill to fund national parks, programs for Native Americans and other schemes if the bill killed the NEA.
